nodes.label: CBL
nodes.summary: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that acts as a negative regulator of many signaling pathways by mediating ubiquitination of cell surface receptors (PubMed:10514377, PubMed:11896602, PubMed:14661060, PubMed:14739300, PubMed:15190072, PubMed:17509076, PubMed:18374639, PubMed:19689429, PubMed:21596750, PubMed:28381567, PubMed:40101708). Accepts ubiquitin from specific E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzymes, and then transfers it to substrates promoting their degradation by the proteasome (PubMed:10514377, PubMed:14661060, PubMed:14739300, PubMed:17094949, PubMed:17509076, PubMed:17974561). Recognizes activated receptor tyrosine kinases, including KIT, FLT1, FGFR1, FGFR2, PDGFRA, PDGFRB, CSF1R, EPHA8 and KDR and mediates their ubiquitination to terminate signaling (PubMed:15190072, PubMed:18374639, PubMed:21596750). Recognizes membrane-bound HCK, SRC and other kinases of the SRC family and mediates their ubiquitination and degradation (PubMed:11896602). Ubiquitinates EGFR and SPRY2 (PubMed:17094949, PubMed:17974561). Involved in LAG3-mediated inhibition of TCR signaling: following ligand-binding to LAG3, catalyzes 'Lys-63'-linked ubiquitination of LAG3, unleashing the LAG3 C-terminus from the membrane, and initiating a signaling that prevents TCR activation (PubMed:40101708). Ubiquitinates NECTIN1 following association between NECTIN1 and herpes simplex virus 1/HHV-1 envelope glycoprotein D, leading to NECTIN1 removal from cell surface (PubMed:28381567). Participates in signal transduction in hematopoietic cells. Plays an important role in the regulation of osteoblast differentiation and apoptosis (PubMed:15190072, PubMed:18374639). Essential for osteoclastic bone resorption (PubMed:14739300). The 'Tyr-731' phosphorylated form induces the activation and recruitment of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase to the cell membrane in a signaling pathway that is critical for osteoclast function (PubMed:14739300). In association with CBLB, required for proper feedback inhibition of ciliary platelet-derived growth factor receptor-alpha (PDGFRA) signaling pathway via ubiquitination and internalization of PDGFRA (By similarity)

nodes.label: MAP2K1
synonyms: Dual specificity mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase 1
nodes.summary: Dual specificity protein kinase which acts as an essential component of the MAP kinase signal transduction pathway. Binding of extracellular ligands such as growth factors, cytokines and hormones to their cell-surface receptors activates RAS and this initiates RAF1 activation. RAF1 then further activates the dual-specificity protein kinases MAP2K1/MEK1 and MAP2K2/MEK2. Both MAP2K1/MEK1 and MAP2K2/MEK2 function specifically in the MAPK/ERK cascade, and catalyze the concomitant phosphorylation of a threonine and a tyrosine residue in a Thr-Glu-Tyr sequence located in the extracellular signal-regulated kinases MAPK3/ERK1 and MAPK1/ERK2, leading to their activation and further transduction of the signal within the MAPK/ERK cascade. Activates BRAF in a KSR1 or KSR2-dependent manner; by binding to KSR1 or KSR2 releases the inhibitory intramolecular interaction between KSR1 or KSR2 protein kinase and N-terminal domains which promotes KSR1 or KSR2-BRAF dimerization and BRAF activation (PubMed:29433126). Depending on the cellular context, this pathway mediates diverse biological functions such as cell growth, adhesion, survival and differentiation, predominantly through the regulation of transcription, metabolism and cytoskeletal rearrangements. One target of the MAPK/ERK cascade is peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARG), a nuclear receptor that promotes differentiation and apoptosis. MAP2K1/MEK1 has been shown to export PPARG from the nucleus. The MAPK/ERK cascade is also involved in the regulation of endosomal dynamics, including lysosome processing and endosome cycling through the perinuclear recycling compartment (PNRC), as well as in the fragmentation of the Golgi apparatus during mitosis

nodes.label: RAF1
nodes.summary: Serine/threonine-protein kinase that acts as a regulatory link between the membrane-associated Ras GTPases and the MAPK/ERK cascade, and this critical regulatory link functions as a switch determining cell fate decisions including proliferation, differentiation, apoptosis, survival and oncogenic transformation. RAF1 activation initiates a mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) cascade that comprises a sequential phosphorylation of the dual-specific MAPK kinases (MAP2K1/MEK1 and MAP2K2/MEK2) and the extracellular signal-regulated kinases (MAPK3/ERK1 and MAPK1/ERK2). The phosphorylated form of RAF1 (on residues Ser-338 and Ser-339, by PAK1) phosphorylates BAD/Bcl2-antagonist of cell death at 'Ser-75'. Phosphorylates adenylyl cyclases: ADCY2, ADCY5 and ADCY6, resulting in their activation. Phosphorylates PPP1R12A resulting in inhibition of the phosphatase activity. Phosphorylates TNNT2/cardiac muscle troponin T. Can promote NF-kB activation and inhibit signal transducers involved in motility (ROCK2), apoptosis (MAP3K5/ASK1 and STK3/MST2), proliferation and angiogenesis (RB1). Can protect cells from apoptosis also by translocating to the mitochondria where it binds BCL2 and displaces BAD/Bcl2-antagonist of cell death. Regulates Rho signaling and migration, and is required for normal wound healing. Plays a role in the oncogenic transformation of epithelial cells via repression of the TJ protein, occludin (OCLN) by inducing the up-regulation of a transcriptional repressor SNAI2/SLUG, which induces down-regulation of OCLN. Restricts caspase activation in response to selected stimuli, notably Fas stimulation, pathogen-mediated macrophage apoptosis, and erythroid differentiation

nodes.label: MAPK cascade
nodes.summary: An intracellular protein kinase cascade containing at least a MAP kinase (MAPK). It starts with the activation of a MAP3K, and the consecutive activation of a MPK2K and a MAPK. The cascade can also contain an additional tier: the upstream MAP4K. The kinases in each tier phosphorylate and activate the kinase in the downstream tier to transmit a signal within a cell.

nodes.summary: Cholesterol-lowering drugs that reduce RAS-MAPK activity and rescued learning in Nf1+/- mice. Randomised trials in children with NF1 did not improve cognition: a documented failure of pathway-level repurposing.

sources.title: The HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor lovastatin reverses the learning and attention deficits in a mouse model of neurofibromatosis type 1.
sources.quote: We report that lovastatin decreased the enhanced brain p21Ras-MAPK activity of the nf1+/- mice, rescued their LTP deficits, and reversed their spatial learning and attention impairments.

nodes.label: Tipifarnib (farnesyltransferase inhibitor)
nodes.summary: Blocks RAS membrane anchoring by inhibiting farnesylation. A randomised placebo-controlled phase 2 trial in NF1 plexiform neurofibromas did not prolong time to progression: targeting RAS itself failed where targeting MEK later succeeded.

sources.title: R115777 to Treat Children With Neurofibromatosis Type 1 and Progressive Plexiform Neurofibromas [COMPLETED]
sources.quote: R115777 to Treat Children With Neurofibromatosis Type 1 and Progressive Plexiform Neurofibromas

nodes.label: Trametinib (MEK1/2 inhibitor; Mekinist), off-label in RASopathies
nodes.summary: A MEK inhibitor approved for BRAF-mutant cancers. Used off-label for life-threatening hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and lymphatic disease in Noonan syndrome and related RASopathies; a phase 2 randomised trial is recruiting and a phase 3 infant trial is registered.

sources.title: FDA prescribing information (Mekinist), DailyMed set id 0002ad27-779d-42ab-83b5-bc65453412a1, effective 20260507
sources.quote: MEKINIST is a kinase inhibitor indicated as a single agent for the treatment of BRAF-inhibitor treatment-naïve patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with BRAF V600E or V600K mutations

sources.title: Treatment of RAF1-Related Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy by MEK Inhibition Using Trametinib.
sources.quote: We provide the first report of the successful treatment of an adult with RAF1-associated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy using trametinib, a MEK inhibitor.

sources.title: MEK Inhibition in a Newborn with RAF1-Associated Noonan Syndrome Ameliorates Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy but Is Insufficient to Revert Pulmonary Vascular Disease.
sources.quote: Trametinib was introduced (0.022 mg/kg/day) with prompt clinical improvement and subsequent amelioration of HCM at ultrasound.

sources.title: Impact of MEK Inhibition on Childhood RASopathy-Associated Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
sources.quote: A retrospective analysis of 61 patients provides evidence for decreased mortality and morbidity with improved cardiac status in patients with RASopathy with severe hypertrophic cardiomyopathy receiving mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase inhibition (n = 30) vs those with standard-of-care treatment (n = 31).

sources.title: Trametinib for Refractory Chylous Effusions and Systemic Complications in Children with Noonan Syndrome.
sources.quote: RESULTS: Subjects demonstrated improvement in lymphatic leak with additional findings of improved growth and normalization of cardiac and hematologic measurements.

evidence.title: The PTPN11 loss-of-function mutation Q510E-Shp2 causes hypertrophic cardiomyopathy by dysregulating mTOR signaling.

counter_evidence.title: Randomized placebo-controlled study of lovastatin in children with neurofibromatosis type 1.

counter_evidence.title: MEK Inhibition in a Newborn with RAF1-Associated Noonan Syndrome Ameliorates Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy but Is Insufficient to Revert Pulmonary Vascular Disease.
counter_evidence.quote: While MEK-inhibition appears a promising therapeutic option for HCM in RASopathies, it appears insufficient to revert pulmonary hypertension.

evidence.quote: Because of a lack of other treatment options, an expanded access approval was obtained, and the patient initiated treatment by mitogen-activated protein kinase inhibition using trametinib.

edges.label: driven by
edges.explanation: Published work links BRAF-related disorders (Cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome 1) to gain of function. CFC-causing BRAF missense changes activate B-Raf. KRAS and BRAF mutations in CFC: one shared pathway with Noonan and Costello syndromes. Orphanet's curated gene-disease record also annotates this mechanism.

evidence.title: Germline mutations in genes within the MAPK pathway cause cardio-facio-cutaneous syndrome.
evidence.quote: Of the 11 mutations identified, two result in amino acid substitutions that occur in tumors, but most are unique and suggest previously unknown mechanisms of B-Raf activation.

evidence.title: Germline KRAS and BRAF mutations in cardio-facio-cutaneous syndrome.
evidence.quote: In 43 individuals with CFC, we identified two heterozygous KRAS mutations in three individuals and eight BRAF mutations in 16 individuals, suggesting that dysregulation of the RAS-RAF-ERK pathway is a common molecular basis for the three related disorders.

evidence.title: Orphanet ORPHA:1340 Cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome: BRAF - Disease-causing germline mutation(s) (gain of function) in

edges.label: driven by
edges.explanation: Published work links CBL-related disorders (Noonan syndrome-like disorder with or without JMML) to loss of function. Germline CBL missense changes impair the E3 ligase that switches receptor signalling off. Leukaemia in carriers needs loss of the remaining normal allele (a second hit).

evidence.title: Heterozygous germline mutations in the CBL tumor-suppressor gene cause a Noonan syndrome-like phenotype.
evidence.quote: Mutations were shown to affect CBL-mediated receptor ubiquitylation and dysregulate signal flow through RAS.

evidence.title: Germline CBL mutations cause developmental abnormalities and predispose to juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia.
evidence.quote: Importantly, JMML specimens from affected children show loss of the normal CBL allele through acquired isodisomy.

applies_to_subtypes: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with or without JMML

edges.label: driven by
edges.explanation: Published work links HRAS-related disorders (Costello syndrome) to gain of function. Costello syndrome HRAS changes are the same activating changes found in tumours. Orphanet's curated gene-disease record also annotates this mechanism.

evidence.title: Germline mutations in HRAS proto-oncogene cause Costello syndrome.
evidence.quote: We identified four heterozygous de novo mutations of HRAS in 12 of 13 affected individuals, all of which were previously reported as somatic and oncogenic mutations in various tumors.

evidence.title: Orphanet ORPHA:3071 Costello syndrome: HRAS - Disease-causing germline mutation(s) (gain of function) in

edges.label: driven by
edges.explanation: Published work links KRAS-related disorders (Noonan syndrome 3) to gain of function. KRAS Noonan mutants hydrolyse GTP poorly and escape GAP control: hyperactive Ras. Orphanet's curated gene-disease record also annotates this mechanism.

evidence.title: Germline KRAS mutations cause Noonan syndrome.
evidence.quote: Recombinant V14I and T58I K-Ras proteins show defective intrinsic GTP hydrolysis and impaired responsiveness to GTPase activating proteins, render primary hematopoietic progenitors hypersensitive to growth factors and deregulate signal transduction in a cell lineage-specific manner.

evidence.title: Orphanet ORPHA:1340 Cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome: KRAS - Disease-causing germline mutation(s) (gain of function) in

edges.label: driven by
edges.explanation: Published work links LZTR1-related disorders (LZTR1-related schwannomatosis / isolated cafe-au-lait macules; Noonan syndrome 10 (dominant); Noonan syndrome 2 (recessive); Noonan syndrome 2 / 10) to loss of function. LZTR1 tags RAS for ubiquitination; disease mutations break this. Independent screen: LZTR1 loss raises membrane KRAS and MAPK activity.

evidence.title: Mutations in LZTR1 drive human disease by dysregulating RAS ubiquitination.
evidence.quote: Disease-associated LZTR1 mutations disrupted either LZTR1-CUL3 complex formation or its interaction with RAS proteins.

evidence.title: LZTR1 is a regulator of RAS ubiquitination and signaling.
evidence.quote: Inactivation of LZTR1 led to decreased ubiquitination and enhanced plasma membrane localization of endogenous KRAS (V-Ki-ras2 Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog).

evidence.title: Autosomal recessive Noonan syndrome associated with biallelic LZTR1 variants.
evidence.quote: CONCLUSION: These clinical and genetic data confirm the existence of a form of Noonan syndrome that is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern and identify biallelic mutations in LZTR1.

evidence.title: Heterozygosity for loss-of-function variants in LZTR1 is associated with isolated multiple café-au-lait macules.
evidence.quote: The molecular spectrum mainly consisted of truncating variants, indicating loss-of-function.

evidence.title: Dominant Noonan syndrome-causing LZTR1 mutations specifically affect the Kelch domain substrate-recognition surface and enhance RAS-MAPK signaling.
evidence.quote: We provide the first evidence that these mutations, but not the missense changes occurring as biallelic mutations in recessive NS, enhance stimulus-dependent RAS-MAPK signaling, which is triggered, at least in part, by an increased RAS protein pool.

edges.label: driven by
edges.explanation: Published work links MAP2K1-related disorders (Cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome 3) to gain of function. MEK1/MEK2 missense changes cause CFC in BRAF-negative patients. Limiting or contradicting findings are attached as counter-evidence: The CFC MEK1 variants still depend on RAF phosphorylation: they amplify rather than bypass upstream signalling. Orphanet's curated gene-disease record also annotates this mechanism.

evidence.title: Germline mutations in genes within the MAPK pathway cause cardio-facio-cutaneous syndrome.
evidence.quote: Furthermore, three of five individuals without BRAF mutations had missense mutations in either MEK1 or MEK2, downstream effectors of B-Raf.

evidence.title: Orphanet ORPHA:1340 Cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome: MAP2K1 - Disease-causing germline mutation(s) (gain of function) in

counter_evidence.title: Germline mutations of MEK in cardio-facio-cutaneous syndrome are sensitive to MEK and RAF inhibition: implications for therapeutic options.
counter_evidence.quote: Our CFC MEK variants cannot induce ERK unless they are phosphorylated by RAF at two key serine residues in the regulatory loop.

edges.label: driven by
edges.explanation: Published work links NF1-related disorders (Neurofibromatosis type 1) to loss of function. Neurofibromin is a RAS GTPase-activating protein; losing it leaves RAS switched on. Nf1+/- mice: learning deficits come from excess Ras activity. Orphanet's curated gene-disease record also annotates this mechanism.

evidence.title: Neurofibromin and suppression of tumorigenesis: beyond the GAP.
evidence.quote: The NF1 gene encodes neurofibromin, a large protein with RAS GTP-ase activating (RAS-GAP) activity, and loss of NF1 results in increased RAS signaling.

evidence.title: The HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor lovastatin reverses the learning and attention deficits in a mouse model of neurofibromatosis type 1.
evidence.quote: A previous study showed that the learning and memory deficits of a mouse model of NF1 (nf1+/-) appear to be caused by excessive p21Ras activity leading to impairments in long-term potentiation (LTP), a cellular mechanism of learning and memory.

evidence.title: Orphanet ORPHA:363700 Neurofibromatosis type 1 due to NF1 mutation or intragenic deletion: NF1 - Disease-causing germline mutation(s) (loss of function) in

edges.label: driven by
edges.explanation: Published work links PTPN11-related disorders (Noonan syndrome with multiple lentigines (LEOPARD syndrome 1)) to a dominant-negative effect. NSML (LEOPARD) mutants are catalytically defective and dominant negative, unlike Noonan mutants. The recurrent NSML substitutions Y279C and T468M abolish catalytic activity. Limiting or contradicting findings are attached as counter-evidence: Kinetic and structural work argues NSML mutants can still behave as gain of function in cells.

evidence.title: PTPN11 (Shp2) mutations in LEOPARD syndrome have dominant negative, not activating, effects.
evidence.quote: Surprisingly, we found that in marked contrast to NS, LS mutants are catalytically defective and act as dominant negative mutations that interfere with growth factor/Erk-mitogen-activated protein kinase-mediated signaling.

evidence.title: Diversity and functional consequences of germline and somatic PTPN11 mutations in human disease.
evidence.quote: Furthermore, we show that the recurrent LS-causing Y279C and T468M amino acid substitutions engender loss of SHP-2 catalytic activity, identifying a previously unrecognized behavior for this class of missense PTPN11 mutations.

evidence.title: Rapamycin reverses hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in a mouse model of LEOPARD syndrome-associated PTPN11 mutation.
evidence.quote: Our results demonstrate that LS mutations have dominant-negative effects in vivo, identify enhanced mTOR activity as critical for causing LS-associated HCM, and suggest that TOR inhibitors be considered for treatment of HCM in LS patients.

counter_evidence.title: Molecular basis of gain-of-function LEOPARD syndrome-associated SHP2 mutations.
counter_evidence.quote: Consequently, catalytically impaired SHP2 mutants could display gain-of-function properties because of their ability to localize to the vicinity of substrates for longer periods of time, thereby affording the opportunity for prolonged substrate turnover and sustained RAS-ERK1/2 activation.

applies_to_subtypes: Noonan syndrome with multiple lentigines (LEOPARD syndrome 1)

edges.label: driven by
edges.explanation: Published work links PTPN11-related disorders (Noonan syndrome 1) to gain of function. Discovery paper: Noonan-causing PTPN11 missense changes favour the active SHP-2 conformation. Noonan mutations are activating, but milder than leukemia-associated ones.

evidence.title: Mutations in PTPN11, encoding the protein tyrosine phosphatase SHP-2, cause Noonan syndrome.
evidence.quote: This implies that they are gain-of-function changes and that the pathogenesis of Noonan syndrome arises from excessive SHP-2 activity.

evidence.title: Diversity and functional consequences of germline and somatic PTPN11 mutations in human disease.
evidence.quote: Our results document a strict correlation between the identity of the lesion and disease and demonstrate that NS-causative mutations have less potency for promoting SHP-2 gain of function than do leukemia-associated ones.

edges.label: driven by
edges.explanation: Published work links PTPN11-related disorders (Metachondromatosis) to loss of function. Truncating and splice PTPN11 variants cause metachondromatosis, with a second hit in lesions. Orphanet's curated gene-disease record also annotates this mechanism.

evidence.title: Loss-of-function mutations in PTPN11 cause metachondromatosis, but not Ollier disease or Maffucci syndrome.
evidence.quote: We conclude that heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in PTPN11 are a frequent cause of MC, that lesions in patients with MC appear to arise following a "second hit," that MC may be locus heterogeneous since 1 familial and 5 sporadically occurring cases lacked obvious disease-causing PTPN11 mutations, and that PTPN11 mutations are not a common cause of Ollier disease or Maffucci syndrome.

edges.label: driven by

HCM-hotspot RAF1 mutants are kinase-activating; non-HCM mutants are kinase impaired, so the gain-of-function label holds best for the HCM-associated alleles. Orphanet's curated gene-disease record also annotates this mechanism.

evidence.title: Germline gain-of-function mutations in RAF1 cause Noonan syndrome.
evidence.quote: Thus, our findings implicate RAF1 gain-of-function mutations as a causative agent of a human developmental disorder, representing a new genetic mechanism for the activation of the MAPK pathway.

evidence.title: Gain-of-function RAF1 mutations cause Noonan and LEOPARD syndromes with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
evidence.quote: Ectopically expressed RAF1 mutants from the two HCM hotspots had increased kinase activity and enhanced ERK activation, whereas non-HCM-associated mutants were kinase impaired.

evidence.title: MEK-ERK pathway modulation ameliorates disease phenotypes in a mouse model of Noonan syndrome associated with the Raf1(L613V) mutation.
evidence.quote: These data show that different NS genes have intrinsically distinct pathological effects, demonstrate that enhanced MEK-ERK activity is critical for causing HCM and other RAF1-mutant NS phenotypes, and suggest a mutation-specific approach to the treatment of RASopathies.

evidence.title: Gain-of-function mutations in RIT1 cause Noonan syndrome, a RAS/MAPK pathway syndrome.

edges.label: Loss of RAS regulation (negative regulators lost)
edges.explanation: Both genes encode RAS 'off-switches' (neurofibromin, a RAS GAP; CBL, an E3 ubiquitin ligase); losing them leaves RAS signalling on, and the CBL discovery paper explicitly likens the disorder to NF1.

evidence.title: Neurofibromin and suppression of tumorigenesis: beyond the GAP.
evidence.quote: The NF1 gene encodes neurofibromin, a large protein with RAS GTP-ase activating (RAS-GAP) activity, and loss of NF1 results in increased RAS signaling.

evidence.title: Germline CBL mutations cause developmental abnormalities and predispose to juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia.
evidence.quote: We conclude that germline CBL mutations have developmental, tumorigenic and functional consequences that resemble disorders that are caused by hyperactive Ras/Raf/MEK/ERK signaling and include neurofibromatosis type 1, Noonan syndrome, Costello syndrome, cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome and Legius syndrome.

evidence.title: Heterozygous germline mutations in the CBL tumor-suppressor gene cause a Noonan syndrome-like phenotype.
evidence.quote: Mutations were shown to affect CBL-mediated receptor ubiquitylation and dysregulate signal flow through RAS.

attrs.basis: loss of a RAS off-switch (GAP / E3 ubiquitin ligase)

edges.label: Loss of RAS regulation (negative regulators lost)
edges.explanation: Both genes encode RAS 'off-switches' (neurofibromin, a RAS GAP; LZTR1, which tags RAS for ubiquitination); loss of either increases RAS signalling and both predispose to nerve-sheath tumours (neurofibromas / schwannomas).

evidence.title: Neurofibromin and suppression of tumorigenesis: beyond the GAP.
evidence.quote: The NF1 gene encodes neurofibromin, a large protein with RAS GTP-ase activating (RAS-GAP) activity, and loss of NF1 results in increased RAS signaling.

evidence.title: Mutations in LZTR1 drive human disease by dysregulating RAS ubiquitination.
evidence.quote: LZTR1-mediated ubiquitination inhibited RAS signaling by attenuating its association with the membrane.

evidence.title: Heterozygosity for loss-of-function variants in LZTR1 is associated with isolated multiple café-au-lait macules.
evidence.quote: PURPOSE: Pathogenic LZTR1 variants cause schwannomatosis and dominant/recessive Noonan syndrome (NS).

attrs.basis: loss of a RAS off-switch (GAP / CUL3-LZTR1 ubiquitination)

edges.label: MEK-inhibitor-responsive MAPK overactivation
edges.explanation: Different genes, one pathway, one drug class: NF1 plexiform neurofibromas are driven by elevated RAS-MAPK signalling and respond to MEK inhibitors (approved); RAF1 hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is driven by enhanced MEK-ERK activity and has responded to the MEK inhibitor trametinib in case reports and in Raf1 mice. Pulmonary vascular disease did not respond in one infant (counter-evidence).

evidence.title: Activity of Selumetinib in Neurofibromatosis Type 1-Related Plexiform Neurofibromas.
evidence.quote: BACKGROUND: Effective medical therapies are lacking for the treatment of neurofibromatosis type 1-related plexiform neurofibromas, which are characterized by elevated RAS-mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling.

evidence.title: MEK-ERK pathway modulation ameliorates disease phenotypes in a mouse model of Noonan syndrome associated with the Raf1(L613V) mutation.
evidence.quote: These data show that different NS genes have intrinsically distinct pathological effects, demonstrate that enhanced MEK-ERK activity is critical for causing HCM and other RAF1-mutant NS phenotypes, and suggest a mutation-specific approach to the treatment of RASopathies.

evidence.title: Treatment of RAF1-Related Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy by MEK Inhibition Using Trametinib.
evidence.quote: RASopathies cause nonsarcomeric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy via dysregulated signaling through RAS and upregulated mitogen-activated protein kinase activity.

counter_evidence.title: MEK Inhibition in a Newborn with RAF1-Associated Noonan Syndrome Ameliorates Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy but Is Insufficient to Revert Pulmonary Vascular Disease.
counter_evidence.quote: While MEK-inhibition appears a promising therapeutic option for HCM in RASopathies, it appears insufficient to revert pulmonary hypertension.

attrs.basis: mapk-overactivation; MEK inhibitor approved for NF1 tried for RAF1 HCM

edges.label: MEK-inhibitor-responsive MAPK overactivation
edges.explanation: NF1 tumours and RIT1 Noonan cardiomyopathy share RAS/MAPK overactivation; the MEK-inhibitor class approved for NF1 resolved RIT1-associated HCM in a case report.

evidence.title: Activity of Selumetinib in Neurofibromatosis Type 1-Related Plexiform Neurofibromas.
evidence.quote: BACKGROUND: Effective medical therapies are lacking for the treatment of neurofibromatosis type 1-related plexiform neurofibromas, which are characterized by elevated RAS-mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling.

evidence.title: Succesful MEK-inhibition of severe hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in RIT1-related Noonan Syndrome.
evidence.quote: Meanwhile, several approved agents targeting the same RAS/MAPK signaling pathway are used in cancer treatment.

evidence.title: Gain-of-function mutations in RIT1 cause Noonan syndrome, a RAS/MAPK pathway syndrome.
evidence.quote: These results demonstrate that gain-of-function mutations in RIT1 cause Noonan syndrome and show a similar biological effect to mutations in other RASopathy-related genes.

attrs.basis: mapk-overactivation; MEK inhibitor approved for NF1 tried for RIT1 HCM

clusters.label: RASopathies: one signalling pathway turned up
clusters.rationale: Twelve genes, many diagnoses (Noonan syndrome, NSML, Costello, cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome, neurofibromatosis type 1, Mazzanti syndrome, CBL syndrome), one pathway: each gene encodes a component or regulator of RAS/MAPK signalling and the vast majority of disease variants increase signalling (PMID:19467855, PMID:23875798, PMID:29924299, PMID:38929714); ClinGen curated the gene set (PMID:30311384). Shared pathway means shared drug targets: MEK inhibitors approved for NF1 are being repurposed across the family.

clusters.label: MEK-inhibitor-responsive RAS/MAPK overactivation
clusters.rationale: Diseases where blocking MEK has been approved (NF1 plexiform neurofibromas: selumetinib, mirdametinib), used off-label with reported benefit (RAF1 and RIT1 hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, SOS1 lymphatic disease) or is being trialled (MEKinRAS phase 2; Baby MERIT phase 3, which admits Noonan/Costello/CFC genes including recessive LZTR1 but excludes NSML-type PTPN11). CFC MEK1 variants are MEK-inhibitor-sensitive in vitro (PMID:17981815) but no clinical report was found. Limits: case-level evidence, one withdrawn 2012 trial, and no completed randomised trial outside NF1.

clusters.label: Loss of RAS regulation (NF1, LZTR1, CBL)
clusters.rationale: Most RASopathy genes are activated accelerators; these three are lost brakes. Neurofibromin is a RAS GTPase-activating protein (PMID:35066574), LZTR1 tags RAS for ubiquitination and removal from the membrane (PMID:30442762, PMID:30442766) and CBL ubiquitylates receptors (PMID:20619386). Loss-of-function variants (truncating, splice, deletions) dominate their ClinVar spectra, and tumour predisposition via a second hit is shared (NF1 neurofibromas, LZTR1 schwannomas, CBL JMML).

clusters.label: Same gene, different mechanism (PTPN11, LZTR1, RAF1)
clusters.rationale: PTPN11 Noonan variants activate SHP2 (PMID:11704759) whereas NSML variants are catalytically defective and dominant negative (PMID:16377799) and truncating variants cause metachondromatosis (PMID:21533187). Therapy follows mechanism: NSML-type PTPN11 is excluded from the infant MEK-inhibitor trial (NCT07817186) and responded to mTOR inhibition in mice (PMID:21339643), with human-tissue caution (PMID:31722741). LZTR1 dominant variants hit substrate recognition while recessive and schwannomatosis alleles are loss of function (PMID:30481304, PMID:39140257). RAF1 HCM-hotspot variants are kinase-activating while others are kinase impaired (PMID:17603483).

gaps.question: Does MEK inhibition improve outcomes in Noonan-spectrum hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or lymphatic disease, beyond case reports?
what_is_missing: No completed randomised or controlled trial outside NF1: MEKinRAS (NCT06555237, phase 2) is recruiting and Baby MERIT (NCT07817186, phase 3) is not yet recruiting.
The first MEK-inhibitor trial in Noonan HCM (binimetinib/MEK162, NCT01556568) was withdrawn 'due to scientific and business considerations' with 0 enrolled.
Clinical evidence is case reports/series and one retrospective 61-patient comparison (PMID:40131150) whose abstract does not break results down by gene.
Pulmonary vascular disease did not respond in a RAF1 infant (PMID:35052347).

gaps.question: What treatment fits NSML-type (catalytically impaired) PTPN11 hypertrophic cardiomyopathy?
what_is_missing: NSML-causing PTPN11 variants are explicitly excluded from the MEK-inhibitor infant trial (NCT07817186).
mTOR inhibition (rapamycin) is preclinical only (PMID:21339643, PMID:22058153); human NSML heart tissue showed attenuated, not enhanced, mTORC1 activity (PMID:31722741).
Whether NSML mutants behave as loss or gain of function in cardiomyocytes is itself contested (PMID:24935154).

gaps.question: Which individual variants are activating, catalytically impaired or loss of function?
what_is_missing: Variant groups are ClinVar consequence classes; PTPN11 missense variants include both activating (Noonan) and catalytically impaired (NSML) alleles, and RAF1 includes kinase-activating and kinase-impaired alleles (PMID:17603483).

Multi-gene CNVs dominate SHOC2, CBL, HRAS and LZTR1 (22q11.2) ClinVar records and get no mechanism edge.
